title: How Russia Is Attacking the Midterms with a Mother Jones Deepfake

reading.body:
This is a synthetic media failure in which a fabricated video was made to look like the output of a real news organisation. The impersonation was carried out at the level of branding and identity: a fake Mother Jones logo and doctored footage of its editor were used to lend a false claim the appearance of reported journalism. The false claim itself, that the DNC paid a specific sum to a named CNN executive for a stated purpose, was asserted as fact inside that borrowed identity.

The distribution path ran through social platforms rather than the outlet's own channels, and the accounts that carried it were identified by researchers as likely bots. Catching this would have required platform-side detection of coordinated inauthentic accounts and of synthetic video, or verification by viewers that the clip existed on Mother Jones's own properties. The outlet's own recourse came after publication, through a trademark complaint that resulted in removal.

What is not established is who exactly operated the network, whether the accounts were bots in fact rather than in researchers' assessment, and what effect the campaign had on voters. The attribution to a Russian network and the assessment of limited reach are findings reported by researchers, not adjudicated conclusions.

reports.title: How Russia Is Attacking the Midterms with a Mother Jones Deepfake

summary:
A Russian disinformation network called Matryoshka or Storm-1679 created a fake Mother Jones video claiming the Democratic National Committee paid $259 million to CNN chief Mark Thompson to promote gender transition among children. The video used a fake Mother Jones logo and doctored footage of editor Clara Jeffery. It spread on X, gaining 155,000 views on one account and 50,000 on another. Researchers identified the accounts as likely bots. The campaign also produced deepfakes of celebrities like Sarah Jessica Parker and Julia Roberts urging votes for Republicans.

Mother Jones complained to X, which removed the video for violating its trademark policy. The operation targets the 2026 midterms and appears designed to help Trump and the GOP. Researchers say its reach so far is limited, but similar Russian campaigns spread widely in 2024. The article notes the Trump administration has closed government units that once tracked foreign disinformation, leaving the US less able to counter such operations.
